row.stop_reason: Exercise is completely confounded with time of sacrifice / tissue-collection session: every exercised animal (SWIM, SWW) was sacrificed at 13.5 wk post-surgery and every sedentary CONT SCI animal at 11.5 wk (GEO 'weeks after injury', S2.3.p1, S4.3.p1). No sedentary animal shares the exercised animals' collection time, so wpi cannot be adjusted and the exercise contrast cannot be separated from 2 extra weeks post-injury, ~2 weeks of age, and a separate collection session. The data show the confound dominates: on log2 CPM of the 500 most variable genes, PC1 (57% of variance; paper Fig 3b reports 66%) puts CONT (-14.6) with No SCI (-14.3) and puts SWIM (+9.9), SWW (+10.5) together with TX SCI (+10.7), which was collected at yet another time (8.5 wk). Mild swimming/wading and complete transection producing the same dominant shift while contusion vs no injury produces none fits a collection-session effect, not exercise biology. The paper's argument that batch effects are unlikely (S4.3.p1) is an assumption, not a design control. Exercise vs no-exercise is therefore not identifiable from GSE125630. The runner's suitability report independently fails the covariance check (wpi: primary_nested_in_candidate with grp; GSE125630/suitability/suitability.md).
